generations.prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit. Asset type: production pixel-art BODY sprite sheet for a top-down 2.5D survival game, NOT an illustration.
Edit the attached template sheet for ONE character: a scavenger in a dark gray-olive cap and a sand-brown work coat, dark trousers, worn boots and a small backpack.
The sheet has THREE equal columns and FIVE equal rows, 768 by 1920 pixels. Each cell is 256 by 384 and represents a 32 by 48 logical-pixel sprite at exactly 8x nearest-neighbor enlargement. Rows top-to-bottom face EAST (screen-right profile), SOUTHEAST (down-right three-quarter), SOUTH (front toward viewer), NORTHEAST (up-right rear three-quarter), NORTH (back away). Every column in a row keeps exactly that direction.
Column 0 already holds the character's current idle pose. Keep column 0 pixel-for-pixel unchanged.
Column 1: HIT REACTION key pose, the same character a split second after a bullet strikes: shoulders hunched in, head ducked one or two logical pixels and tucked, torso tightened, knees slightly bent. Direction-neutral: no strong forward or backward lean, because the hit can come from any side (the game adds its own 2-pixel knock along the shot). Loose cloth, cap, straps or the backpack may swing one or two logical pixels to sell the impact.
Column 2: RECOVERY pose, halfway between column 1 and the idle pose of column 0.
Anchors: boots' soles stay at logical y=47 on the same bottom-centre foot anchor (x=16) as column 0; the whole body may sink at most one logical pixel. Keep the shoulder line within one logical pixel of column 0 (about logical y=19) and the body centre within one logical pixel of x=16: the game draws articulated arms from the shoulders to the held weapon at logical y=26.
BODY LAYER ONLY, exactly the parts column 0 shows: head, torso, existing sleeves, carried bags and straps, pelvis, legs and boots. Do not add forearms reaching out, hands or weapons.
Same character, palette, one-logical-pixel outline, soft upper-left light and pixel clusters as column 0; clear large shapes readable at 32 by 48. Not cute/chibi, not smooth painted.
No blood, wounds, text, ground, shadows, motion lines, effects, gutters, labels or grid lines. Background must be truly transparent, not a checkerboard. Do not crop any figure; every body stays inside its cell.
Production constraints: use the supplied image as an in-place template with the SAME original canvas, exact cell positions and original sprite scale. Fill all ten blank cells, do not rearrange or enlarge the figures. Lock column 0 completely. Each new pixel cluster uses the exact same 8 by 8 logical-pixel lattice as column 0; do not add fine detail or antialiasing. Keep the same boots and sole positions as the reference in each row. Respect all five distinct view directions. Recovery must visibly differ from both idle and hurt.
